text:
Mackie Samoskevich came to Seattle with a Stanley Cup ring from Florida and has quietly become one of the Kraken's more useful forwards: 6 goals and 15 points in 20 games, nine of them in his last ten, on about 16 minutes a night.

The interesting split is between his shot share and his chance share. At 5v5 Seattle gets only 45% of the shot attempts with him on the ice but 50% of the expected goals, more than six points better than without him. He's not winning possession; he's winning the quality battle, which fits Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season: 53% of his shots came off the rush and 70% of his exits left the zone with the puck. Evolving-Hockey had his teams creating 0.19 more expected goals per 60 with him out there (90th percentile among forwards).

Some regression is due. He's shooting 15.8% against a likely range of 10 to 14%, and his points rate (2.9 per 60) sits well above the 2.0 we'd expect. The rush game is real; the finishing is running hot.
